```lean
Module.End.genEigenspace.{v, w} {R : Type v} {M : Type w} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (f : End R M)
  (μ : R) : ℕ →o Submodule R M
```
***
The generalized eigenspace for a linear map `f`, a scalar `μ`, and an exponent `k ∈ ℕ` is the
kernel of `(f - μ • id) ^ k`. (Def 8.10 of [axler2015]). Furthermore, a generalized eigenspace for
some exponent `k` is contained in the generalized eigenspace for exponents larger than `k`. 
***

```lean
Module.End.IsSemisimple.{u_1, u_2} {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
  (f : End R M) : Prop
```
***
A linear endomorphism of an `R`-module `M` is called *semisimple* if the induced `R[X]`-module
structure on `M` is semisimple. This is equivalent to saying that every `f`-invariant `R`-submodule
of `M` has an `f`-invariant complement: see `Module.End.isSemisimple_iff`. 
***

```
***
An element is said to be nilpotent if some natural-number-power of it equals zero.

Note that we require only the bare minimum assumptions for the definition to make sense. Even
`MonoidWithZero` is too strong since nilpotency is important in the study of rings that are only
power-associative.

```lean
rfl.{u} {α : Sort u} {a : α} : a = a
```
***
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.

  (f : End R M) : Prop
```
***
A linear endomorphism of an `R`-module `M` is called *semisimple* if the induced `R[X]`-module
structure on `M` is semisimple. This is equivalent to saying that every `f`-invariant `R`-submodule
of `M` has an `f`-invariant complement: see `Module.End.isSemisimple_iff`. 
***
*import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Semisimple*

  (μ : R) : ℕ →o Submodule R M
```
***
The generalized eigenspace for a linear map `f`, a scalar `μ`, and an exponent `k ∈ ℕ` is the
kernel of `(f - μ • id) ^ k`. (Def 8.10 of [axler2015]). Furthermore, a generalized eigenspace for
some exponent `k` is contained in the generalized eigenspace for exponents larger than `k`.

***

such that `f x = μ • x`. (Def 5.36 of [axler2015])

```lean
rfl.{u} {α : Sort u} {a : α} : a = a
```
***
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
